questions.q: What was Passepartout doing on the platform when the strange man appeared?
choices: Working out the value of the golden-looking sun in pounds
Counting the cars of the train as it went around a curve
Watching for herds of buffalo out on the snowy prairie
Writing a letter home to his friends in Paris
questions.evidence: calculating its value in pounds sterling

questions.q: What was the stranger wearing that made him look like a clergyman?
choices: A long grey coat and a red scarf
Black clothes and a white cravat
A brown suit and a straw hat
A blue uniform with brass buttons
questions.evidence: a black waistcoat, black trousers, a white cravat

questions.q: What did the stranger fix to the door of each car?
choices: A printed timetable
A handwritten notice
A map of Utah
A warning about thieves
questions.evidence: affixed to the door of each car a notice written in manuscript

choices: A lecture by Elder William Hitch in car No. 117
A dinner party for passengers in the saloon car
A change in the train's stopping time at Ogden
A reward for anyone who found a lady's lost purse
questions.evidence: would deliver a lecture on Mormonism in car No. 117

questions.q: Who chose not to go to the lecture?
choices: Passepartout and Aouda
Mr. Fogg and Fix
The conductor and the engineer
Only the women on the train
questions.evidence: Neither Mr. Fogg nor Fix cared to attend.

questions.q: How did Elder Hitch speak when he began his lecture?
choices: Softly, as if telling a bedtime story
In an irritated voice, as if already contradicted
Slowly, reading every word from a small book
Cheerfully, making the audience laugh often
questions.evidence: in an irritated voice, as if he had already been contradicted

questions.q: What happened to the size of the audience as the lecture went on?
choices: More passengers kept crowding into the car
It stayed about the same until the end
People left until only Passepartout remained
Everyone left at once when the train stopped
questions.evidence: Passepartout was now the only person left in the car

questions.q: The Elder's story "became somewhat wearisome." What does wearisome mean?
choices: Frightening
Tiring and dull
Hard to hear
Very amusing to hear
questions.evidence: The Elder's story became somewhat wearisome

questions.q: What did Passepartout answer when the Elder invited him to plant his tent with them?
choices: He said he would think about it
He said "No!" and left the car
He asked to hear more the next day
He said he must first ask Mr. Fogg

questions.q: The Elder was left "to preach to vacancy." What does this mean?
choices: He went on talking to a crowd of new listeners
He was left talking to an empty car
He was asked to give his talk again later
He moved his lecture to another car
questions.evidence: leaving the Elder to preach to vacancy

questions.q: Why can fish not live in the Great Salt Lake, according to the chapter?
choices: The water is far too cold all winter
The water holds a great deal of salt
The lake is frozen solid most of the year
Large birds catch every fish that comes

questions.q: What did Mr. Fogg and his party do during the six-hour stop at Ogden?
choices: They slept for hours at a hotel near the station
They visited Salt Lake City by a branch road
They went hunting buffalo on the prairie
They waited in the car playing whist all day
questions.evidence: Mr. Fogg and his party had time to pay a visit to Salt Lake City

questions.q: How were the streets of Salt Lake City laid out?
choices: In winding circles around a hill
Like a checker-board
Along a single long road
In no plan at all

questions.q: What happened just as the train began to leave Salt Lake station?
choices: A wheel broke and the train had to stop for repairs
A man ran shouting "Stop!" and jumped onto the rear platform
Fix got off the train and disappeared into the crowd
Elder Hitch began a second lecture in the dining car
questions.evidence: jumped on the rear platform of the train

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Passepartout hearing a long lecture on the train and the party visiting Salt Lake City
Passepartout missing the train in Utah and walking to catch up with his master
Fogg arguing with a missionary and being forced to leave the train at Ogden in a snowstorm
The travellers being snowed in at the Great Salt Lake for several days
questions.evidence: Passepartout took one of the front seats
